chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumaydani narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three [characteristics] for whoever possesses them, four [rights] become incumbent upon the people: Whoever, when he speaks to them, does not lie to them; and when he associates with them, does not oppress them; and when he makes a promise to them, does not break it. It becomes incumbent that his justice be manifest among the people, and his chivalry be manifest among them, and that his backbiting be forbidden to them, and that brotherhood be incumbent upon them.

key_terms.غَيْبَتُهُ: His backbiting (talking about someone in their absence)

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that make four rights incumbent upon people towards an individual?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq links these three personal virtues—truthfulness in narration, fairness in companionship, and fidelity in promises—to the jurisprudential concept of 'ijbab' (incumbency), establishing a social contract where the community is religiously bound to uphold the individual's status. This hadith highlights the transition from personal piety to communal recognition, emphasizing that consistent ethical behavior grants a person 'adalah' (justice/integrity) and 'murua' (chivalry), thereby protecting them from 'ghiba' (backbiting) and obligating 'ukhuwwah' (brotherhood).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-29 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Abi Ja’far al-Kumaydany quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

Four things are incumbent to do for anyone who has the following three characteristics: one who doesn’t lie to the people when he talks; one who doesn’t oppress the people in his dealings with them; one who doesn’t act opposite to what he promises. Such a person has perfect chivalry and justice. It is incumbent support his justness; to act like a brother with him; support his justness; not gossip about him; treat him like a brother.”
